summary: Dublin captivates visitors with its Georgian architecture, world-class pubs, and literary heritage that inspired Joyce and Wilde. The vibrant capital blends historic sites like Trinity College and the Guinness Storehouse with contemporary culture, exceptional food scene, and riverside walks along the Liffey.

restaurants.name: Leo Burdock
restaurants.description: Dublin's most famous fish and chips shop, operating since 1952 in a tiny storefront. Locals queue for crispy battered fish with perfectly salted chips.
restaurants.mustTry: Traditional fish and chips with mushy peas

restaurants.name: The Winding Stair
restaurants.description: Cozy bookstore restaurant overlooking the Liffey with seasonal Irish cuisine using local produce. Intimate atmosphere with exposed brick and literary charm.
restaurants.mustTry: Irish lamb stew with soda bread

restaurants.name: Shanahan's on the Green
restaurants.description: Elegant American steakhouse on St. Stephen's Green featuring dry-aged beef and an extensive wine list. Classic fine dining with attentive service.

restaurants.name: Café Noir
restaurants.description: Casual French-inspired café perfect for breakfasts and light lunches in the city center. Known for excellent coffee and fresh pastries.

restaurants.name: Proper Order
restaurants.description: Casual fish restaurant in Temple Bar with sustainable seafood and casual vibe. Great value for fresh Dublin Bay prawns and white fish.

restaurants.name: Restaurant Patrick Guilbaud
restaurants.description: Two Michelin-starred restaurant showcasing modern Irish cuisine with French technique in an elegant setting. One of Dublin's most prestigious dining experiences.

restaurants.name: Klaw
restaurants.description: Casual seafood restaurant in Smithfield specializing in oysters, clams, and fresh catches with natural wine pairings. Modern Irish seafood approach.

restaurants.name: Bunsen
restaurants.description: Minimalist burger shop with high-quality grass-fed Irish beef and simple preparation. Fast-casual with excellent value.

restaurants.name: Cornucopia
restaurants.description: Small vegetarian restaurant in the city center with creative daily-changing menu using seasonal vegetables. Intimate with warm atmosphere.

restaurants.name: Fallon & Byrne
restaurants.description: Food hall with multiple vendors offering gourmet sandwiches, Irish charcuterie, and prepared foods. Ground floor features excellent deli items.

restaurants.name: The Pig & Brioche
restaurants.description: French-inspired street food and sandwich shop known for quality ingredients and hearty portions. Popular lunch spot with locals.

restaurants.name: Greenhouse
restaurants.description: One Michelin-starred restaurant featuring contemporary Irish cuisine in an elegant dining room. Innovative tasting menus with seasonal focus.

activities.name: Trinity College Dublin & The Book of Kells
activities.description: Ireland's most prestigious university dating to 1592, featuring the stunning Long Room library with ornate wooden ceiling and millions of books. Home to the illuminated manuscript Book of Kells, a masterpiece of medieval art.

activities.name: Guinness Storehouse
activities.description: Seven-story visitor experience at the historic St. James's Gate brewery where visitors learn the history of Guinness. The Gravity Bar on top offers 360-degree views of Dublin with a complimentary pint.

activities.name: Dublin Literary Pub Crawl
activities.description: Guided walking tour through historic pubs with actors performing scenes from works by Joyce, Beckett, and Wilde. Immersive theater-style experience celebrating Dublin's literary legacy.

activities.name: Christ Church Cathedral & Crypt
activities.description: Medieval cathedral dating to 1172 with stunning architecture and the largest crypt in Ireland containing preserved mummies. Active place of worship with exceptional stonework and stained glass.

activities.name: St. Stephen's Green Walking Tour
activities.description: 22-acre public park in the city center featuring Victorian gardens, fountains, and statues in a peaceful setting. Free to explore with benches and paths perfect for relaxation.

activities.name: Howth Head Coastal Walk
activities.description: Scenic cliff-top walking trail on Dublin's northern peninsula with stunning sea views, seabirds, and photography opportunities. Easy to moderate hike with multiple route options.

activities.name: Temple Bar Food Market & District
activities.description: Historic cobblestone area famous for traditional Irish pubs, live music venues, and weekend food market. Bustling with tourists and locals enjoying authentic Irish pub culture.

activities.name: Irish Museum of Modern Art
activities.description: Contemporary art museum in the historic Royal Hospital Kilmainham featuring Irish and international works. Beautiful Georgian building with peaceful courtyard and free general admission.

activities.name: Liffey River Walk & Bridges
activities.description: Scenic riverside promenade along the Liffey connecting the Quays with views of historic bridges including the iconic Ha'penny Bridge. Free walk through Dublin's heart with excellent photo opportunities.

activities.name: National Museum of Ireland - Archaeology
activities.description: World-class museum featuring Viking treasures, Celtic artifacts, and the famous Broighter Gold. Impressive collection of Irish prehistoric and medieval objects.

activities.name: Kilmainham Gaol Historic Prison
activities.description: Former prison now museum documenting Irish independence movement and historic executions. Powerful historical experience with guided tours revealing 200 years of Irish history.

activities.name: Traditional Irish Music Session
activities.description: Evening of live traditional Irish music in authentic pubs like O'Donoghue's or The Brazen Head. Musicians improvise jigs and reels in intimate, authentic atmosphere.

spots.name: Ha'penny Bridge at Sunrise
spots.description: Iconic iron pedestrian bridge spanning the Liffey with beautiful light reflecting on the water and Georgian buildings in background.
spots.bestTime: Early morning 6-7am for soft golden light

spots.name: Temple Bar at Night
spots.description: Atmospheric cobblestone street lined with ivy-covered buildings, warm pub lights, and reflections on wet streets.

spots.name: Christ Church Cathedral Exterior
spots.description: Medieval architecture with impressive stonework, buttresses, and spires creating dramatic silhouettes.
spots.bestTime: Golden hour 4-6pm for warm wall lighting

spots.name: Dublin Bay from Howth Head
spots.description: Dramatic coastal cliffs dropping to turquoise water with Dublin's urban landscape visible across the bay.
spots.bestTime: Golden hour for warm light on cliffs and water

spots.name: St. Stephen's Green Gates
spots.description: Ornate Victorian iron gates and park entrance with manicured gardens and statues creating layered composition.
spots.bestTime: Mid-morning 10-11am for frontal light on details

spots.name: Liffey Quays Street Photography
spots.description: Urban riverside scenes with pedestrians, street performers, and reflections on wet pavements.
spots.bestTime: Daytime for varied lighting and crowd activity

spots.name: Trinity College Long Room
spots.description: Interior with soaring wooden barrel-vaulted ceiling, floor-to-ceiling bookshelves, and dramatic perspectives.
spots.bestTime: Midday for directional light through windows

spots.name: Seabirds at Howth Head
spots.description: Nesting puffins, guillemots, and razorbills on clifftops with ocean backdrop during breeding season.
spots.bestTime: May-August morning for active birds and soft light

spots.name: Guinness Storehouse Rooftop
spots.description: Elevated 360-degree city views capturing Dublin's urban sprawl, Georgian rooflines, and surrounding hills.
spots.bestTime: Golden hour 4-5:30pm for warm cityscape light

spots.name: River Reflections at Millennium Bridge
spots.description: Modern pedestrian bridge creating strong linear compositions with reflections of buildings and sky in calm Liffey waters.
spots.bestTime: Early morning for calm water and soft light

lensRecommendations: 16-35mm wide angle for architectural details and expansive city views from elevated positions
50mm prime for street photography and intimate scenes with natural perspective
70-200mm telephoto for wildlife at Howth Head and compressed landscape compositions
14mm ultra-wide for interior cathedral and museum spaces with dramatic depth
photography.goldenHourNotes: Dublin's golden hour is particularly stunning in late spring and summer when it extends from 4-7:30pm. The Georgian buildings glow warmly, and the Liffey becomes a ribbon of reflected light. Winter golden hour is shorter (3-4:30pm) but creates dramatic long shadows across cobblestone streets and enhances moody pub interiors.

weather.seasonality: Dublin experiences mild but wet weather year-round with summer (May-September) offering the warmest temperatures (14-19°C) and longest daylight hours. Winter is cold and rainy with frequent overcast days, making photography challenging but creating moody atmospheric conditions.
weather.summary: Dublin has an oceanic climate with cool temperatures rarely dropping below freezing or exceeding 20°C. Rain is frequent throughout the year, so waterproof layers and umbrellas are essential for any visit regardless of season.

hotels.name: Kinlay House Dublin
hotels.description: Friendly hostel with private rooms and dorms in the heart of Temple Bar offering social atmosphere and walking distance to attractions.

hotels.name: The Marker Waterfront Hotel
hotels.description: Contemporary 4-star hotel with rooftop restaurant overlooking the Liffey and Grand Canal, excellent location for both business and leisure travelers.

hotels.name: The Merrion Hotel
hotels.description: Dublin's most prestigious luxury hotel featuring fine dining restaurants, spa, and art collection in an elegant Georgian townhouse setting on St. Stephen's Green.
